```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
library(tidyverse)
library(dcData)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
data("ZipGeography", "ZipDemography")
library(esquisse)
```

## R Markdown

This is an R Markdown document. Markdown is a simple formatting syntax for authoring HTML, PDF, and MS Word documents. For more details on using R Markdown see <http://rmarkdown.rstudio.com>.

When you click the **Knit** button a document will be generated that includes both content as well as the output of any embedded R code chunks within the document. You can embed an R code chunk like this:

```{r}
head(ZipDemography)
head(ZipGeography)

AgeCountPopPerZip <-
  ZipDemography %>%
  select(Under5years, X18yearsandover, X65yearsandover, Totalpopulation,ZIP) %>%
  left_join(
    ZipGeography %>%
      select(State, ZIP), 
      by = c("ZIP" = "ZIP")) %>%
  
  group_by(State) %>%
  summarise(
    X5yearsto18 = sum(Totalpopulation - Under5years - X18yearsandover, na.rm = TRUE),
    Under5years = sum(Under5years, na.rm = TRUE),
    X18yearsto65 = sum(X18yearsandover - X65yearsandover, na.rm = TRUE),
    X65yearsandover = sum(X65yearsandover, na.rm = TRUE)
    ) %>%
  
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(Under5years, X5yearsto18, X18yearsto65, X65yearsandover),
    names_to = "AgeGroup",
    values_to = "Count"
  )

ggplot(AgeCountPopPerZip) +
 aes(x = AgeGroup, y = Count, fill = AgeGroup) +
 geom_col() +
 scale_fill_hue(direction = 1) +
 theme_minimal() +
 facet_wrap(vars(State))


```

## Including Plots

You can also embed plots, for example:

```{r pressure, echo=FALSE}
plot(pressure)
```

Note that the `echo = FALSE` parameter was added to the code chunk to prevent printing of the R code that generated the plot.
